what: The Tao #179 sublevel campaign (Erdős #1038, supremum side). Rational-weight discrete measures on [-1,1] with denominator N are monic degree-N polynomials with roots in [-1,1]; this record holds certified sublevel measures |{|q|<1}| (lower-bound witnesses for sup = 2*sqrt(2), a theorem of Tao, December 2025), certified grid champions, and per-degree branch-and-bound THEOREMS — independent re-decisions of that known theorem: odd degrees 3, 5, 7 fall strictly below 2.82 < 2*sqrt(2); even degrees 4, 6, 8 have supremum in [2*sqrt(2), 2.82845], the left end attained by (x^2-1)^{N/2}. A degree marked failed was ATTEMPTED and refused on its budget, not silently dropped. Every measure is an exact outward enclosure from BigInt Sturm root isolation; every branch-and-bound pruning uses the certified min-product box bound (calibrated: thin boxes reproduce measures to all printed digits).
provenance: Framing: T. Tao, teorth/erdosproblems#179 (16 Dec 2025), on erdosproblems.com #1038. The SUPREMUM is settled: Tao proved sup = 2*sqrt(2), the two-atom measure the only case of equality (forum thread 1038, 21 Dec 2025; notes of 22 and 27 Dec 2025, Theorem 2.1; formal-conjectures erdos_1038.parts.ii "research solved"), before this campaign ran. The INFIMUM is open on erdosproblems.com (parts.i "research open"); Darvas-Peng-Tao (July 2026) is one of three AI-assisted proof claims for it. This campaign addresses the supremum side only. Sources pinned in corpus/sources/erdos1038. (Corrected 2026-10-05: this field said the infimum side was resolved by Darvas-Peng-Tao.)

cubicChampion.note: interior critical root — the best certified degree-3 value in the record is at r = 201/256, not at a lattice point, near 2.7542: a lower bound on the degree-3 supremum (that it is the maximum is not certified)

quinticPeak.note: the family (x^2-1)^2(x-r) peaks near r = 905/1024 while its sublevel set is one interval, then descends steeply but continuously as a gap opens and the set splits in two (corrected 2026-10-05: this note said it drops discontinuously; for fixed degree the measure is continuous in the roots)
